name: cl-orchestration
description: Coordinates the issues of several projects from one session: worker jobs, reviews and merge checks, and a handoff file that a cleared or compacted coordinator resumes from.

rotateAtTokens.title: Clear an idle coordinator above this many context tokens
rotateAtTokens.description: 200000 by default; 0 turns it off while rotateAtPercent is also 0. Applies only to a session whose project folder (where Claude Code started) holds the handoff file of /cl-orchestration:orchestrating-projects (.cedarloom/runs/handoff.md) and whose file names that session's id (a Session: line). When such a coordinator ends a turn with no background task running and its context is above this size, the plugin clears it with /clear and submits a prompt that resumes it from the file; after a clear or compaction it hands the file back. At most one clear every 10 minutes. Without the file nothing happens.

rotateAtPercent.title: Clear an idle coordinator above this percent of the context window
rotateAtPercent.description: 0 (default) is off and rotateAtTokens applies. Above 0, an idle coordinator that keeps the handoff file of /cl-orchestration:orchestrating-projects is cleared with /clear and resumed from the file once its context fills this percent of the model's context window, in place of rotateAtTokens.

runner.title: Runner that starts the workers
runner.description: Empty by default: auto, which takes orca when its Detect step answers, else starts nothing. orca sets it; a set runner that fails its Detect step starts nothing. A run's --runner argument wins.

hub.title: Hub repository for questions and issues (owner/name)
hub.description: Empty by default: no hub. Set the same value as cl-workflow's hub option: a GitHub repository, best a private one. The coordinator files a question in the project's tracker when that is private, else in the hub, else in the local queue; with issuesIn hub, work items live in the hub too.

issuesIn.title: Where project issues live: repo or hub
issuesIn.description: repo by default: each project's work items, follow-up issues and questions live in its own repository (questions never in a public one). hub: in the hub repository, labeled project:<name>. A project's policy file can choose the other with issues.tracker. Without a hub, repo applies.
